APCTT-C01.quote: The initial 3D position is refined by iteratively minimizing the geometric error, the projection accuracy error (a relative assessment of matched point accuracy compared to the best matched points), and the reprojection error (differences between the modeled camera locations using the 3D point locations and the real camera locations).
APCTT-C01.note: Principles of structure-from-motion photogrammetry and satellite-derived bathymetry (p15).

APCTT-C02.quote: The objective of the project is to collect survey-grade elevation data on Majuro Atoll (fig. 1) to create a topographic digital elevation model (DEM) with a 1-meter (m) horizontal resolution and at least 0.30-m vertical root mean square error (RMSE)
APCTT-C02.note: Application: inundation modelling, coastal management and hazard adaptation.

APCTT-C03.quote: Of 71,373 GNSS points, 69,648 (97.5 percent) had SfM point-cloud points within 1 m of each GNSS point location.
APCTT-C03.note: Results of the processing workflow components.

APCTT-C05.quote: The RMSE of the TBDEM over the land area is 0.197 m using over 70,000 Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) real-time kinematic (RTK) survey points for validation, and 1.066 m for Landsat 8 and 1.112 m for WorldView-3 derived bathymetry using over 16,000 and 9,000 lidar bathymetry points, respectively.
APCTT-C05.note: Validated on the atoll against independent field and lidar data.

APCTT-C06.quote: The final topobathymetric digital elevation model (TBDEM) for Majuro Atoll is derived from various data sources, from charts and soundings to UAS and satellite imagery, spanning over 70 years of data collection on different sections of Majuro Atoll, from 1944 to 2016, and covering an area of 599.6 km2 .
APCTT-C06.note: Workflow applied to produce the full atoll model.

APCTT-C07.note: No operational use of the DEM is reported.

APCTT-C08.quote: The Majuro Atoll TBDEM, (1) has a 1-m resolution, (2) covers a total area of 599.6 km2 , (3) is compliant with the IHO (2008) published standards of vertical accuracy for bathymetry, and (4) satisfies the USGS National Geospatial Program (NGP) lidar base specifications (Heidemann, 2014) for quality level 3 data for topography
APCTT-C08.note: Literal reading: the final product was checked against published standards. Ladder gap: C07 is not shown, so the TRL opinion stays 6.

APCTT-C10.quote: The Majuro Atoll TBDEM, (1) has a 1-m resolution, (2) covers a total area of 599.6 km2 , (3) is compliant with the IHO (2008) published standards of vertical accuracy for bathymetry, and (4) satisfies the USGS National Geospatial Program (NGP) lidar base specifications (Heidemann, 2014) for quality level 3 data for topography
APCTT-C10.note: Measured accuracy (0.197 m RMSE) compared with the stated 0.30 m objective and published standards, and met.

APCTT-C11.quote: To minimize interpolation artifacts, the priority of input topographic SfM and bathymetric SOPAC, SDB, and chart sounding data were determined based on a variety of project data requirements, such as quality, age, accuracy, and coverage.
APCTT-C11.note: Data sources, processing thresholds (p14) and field survey dates (p13) described.

APCTT-C12.quote: The final topobathymetric digital elevation model (TBDEM) for Majuro Atoll is derived from various data sources, from charts and soundings to UAS and satellite imagery, spanning over 70 years of data collection on different sections of Majuro Atoll, from 1944 to 2016, and covering an area of 599.6 km2 .
APCTT-C12.note: Evidence concerns the Majuro TBDEM workflow and product.

notes: Agrees with the organizer estimate TRL 6. C08 and C10 are met on a literal reading (compliance with stated standards) while C07 is not: the ladder has a gap.
